'''Douglas Natelson''' is an American physicist specializing in experimental condensed matter physics, with a focus on nanoscale systems. He is the Harry Carothers Wiess Professor of Physics at [[Rice University]], where he also serves as Associate Dean for Research in the [[Wiess School of Natural Sciences]]. Additionally, Natelson holds courtesy appointments in the departments of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Materials Science and Nanoengineering.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-04 |title=Douglas Natelson {{!}} Faculty {{!}} The People of Rice {{!}} Rice University |url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/douglas-natelson |access-date=2025-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004232049/https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/douglas-natelson |archive-date=4 October 2024 }}</ref>

== Education ==
Douglas Natelson earned his Bachelor of Science in engineering (BSE) in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from [[Princeton University]] in 1993, graduating [[summa cum laude]]. He also obtained a certificate in Engineering Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Doug Natelson (Rice University): Condensed and Living Matter Seminar |url=https://quiest.engineering.upenn.edu/event/condensed-and-living-matter-seminar-by-doug-natelson-rice-university/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=quiest.seas.upenn.edu}}</ref> He then pursued a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in experimental condensed matter physics at [[Stanford University]], completing his doctoral studies in 1998 under the supervision of [[Douglas Osheroff]], a Nobel laureate in Physics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Osheroff |first1=Douglas |last2=Rogge |first2=Sven |last3=Natelson |first3=Douglas |date=1996-06-01 |title=Interactions between active defects in glasses at low temperatures |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02548143 |journal=Czechoslovak Journal of Physics |language=en |volume=46 |issue=6 |pages=3295–3302 |doi=10.1007/BF02548143 |issn=1572-9486|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His dissertation focused on the dielectric, acoustic, and thermal properties of tunneling two-level systems in glasses at ultralow temperatures.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Natelson |first1=Douglas |title=Collective behavior of tunneling systems in amorphous solids |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/304454665 |website=Proquest |access-date=23 September 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
Following his Ph.D., Natelson worked as a postdoctoral researcher at [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]] from 1998 to 2000, where he investigated nanoscale transport and device physics. In 2000, he joined the faculty at [[Rice University]] as an assistant professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy. He was promoted to associate professor in 2006 and full professor in 2010.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}

Natelson has held multiple leadership roles at Rice, including serving as Chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy from 2016 to 2022. In 2022, he briefly served as Interim Vice President for Research at Rice.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Interim Vice Provost for Research Named |url=https://provost.rice.edu/communications/interim-vice-provost-research-named?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Rice University Office of the Provost}}</ref>{{AI-retrieved source|date=April 2026}} He currently holds the title of Harry Carothers Wiess Professor of Physics and serves as Associate Dean for Research in the Wiess School of Natural Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dean's Office Staff |url=https://naturalsciences.rice.edu/deans-office-staff |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=Wiess School of Natural Sciences {{!}} Rice University |language=en}}</ref> Additionally, he has appointments in the Departments of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Materials Science and Nanoengineering.

His research focuses on nanoscale condensed matter physics, including electronic transport, plasmonics, strong electron correlations, and molecular electronics.

Besides his academic and research contributions, Natelson has engaged in science communication through his blog, ''Nanoscale Views'', where he discusses nanoscience and physics topics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-19 |title=Web life: Nanoscale Views |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/web-life-nanoscale-views/ |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref> He is also the author of the textbook ''Nanostructures and Nanotechnology''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Natelson |first=Douglas |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/nanostructures-and-nanotechnology/20961BB4BAA3F2B57373D9D614243440 |title=Nanostructures and Nanotechnology |date=2015 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-87700-8 |location=Cambridge}}</ref>

== Awards ==
His work has been recognized with numerous honors, including a Sloan Research Fellowship,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Natelson receives prestigious Sloan Research Fellowship |url=https://news2.rice.edu/2004/03/18/natelson-receives-prestigious-sloan-research-fellowship/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=news2.rice.edu}}</ref> a Packard Fellowship,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Natelson, Douglas • The David and Lucile Packard Foundation |url=https://www.packard.org/fellow/natelson-douglas/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=The David and Lucile Packard Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> and a National Science Foundation (NSF) CAREER Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NSF Career Award |url=https://provost.rice.edu/awards/nsf-career-award |website=Rice University Office of the Provost}}</ref> Natelson is also a Fellow of the American Physical Society (APS)<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?award_fellowship%5Bquery%5D=Douglas%20Natelson |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> and the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Six Rice University professors elected AAAS fellows |url=https://news2.rice.edu/2012/11/29/six-rice-university-professors-elected-aaas-fellows-4/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=news2.rice.edu}}</ref>
